incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER - P1 - regen/stream-eu-west - 1718880000
incident-bot: Alert: error rate 42% over 5m for /v1/regen endpoints. Source: tokenstore write failures + model-router 5xxs. Impact: regen failures for ~12% of requests. Pager: https://pager.redwood/incident/1718880000

Maya (oncall): on it. I'm primary for this window. Quick triage shows repeated connection refused to tokenstore replica-2 and higher 5xx from model-router-lb in eu-west. Spike started ~1718879800.

Sam: I'm secondary and available. If you want me to run node-level ops (cordon/drain) or perform snapshot+failover I can take that. Any immediate runbook pointers?

Maya (oncall): Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/ops/runbooks/tokenstore-evictions (see "fast mitigation" section). Steps I'm running now:
```
# quick triage commands (running live)
kubectl -n prod logs deploy/tokenstore-consumer -c main --since=10m | tail -n 80
curl -s http://tokenstore-metrics.eu-west.internal/health
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=tokenstore -o wide
# temporary scale up to buy time
kubectl -n prod scale deploy tokenstore-consumer --replicas=6
```

Leo: I already bumped the model-router ASG in eu-west +2 nodes (manual scale) to add capacity. Also flipped 10% of regen traffic to cached-variant route to reduce write pressure. This is temporary but should lower backend QPS.

Tara: Watching customer regen queues. A few customers seeing retries: cust-73, cust-88, cust-112. Not high volume but visible. ETA for mitigation? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Maya (oncall): After scaling consumers and router nodes, error rate dropped to ~22% (5m window). Tokenstore logs show repeated "connection refused" to tokenstore-replica-2 at 10:12:34 UTC. Planning to cordon node 10.4.2.21 and drain the replica to avoid more failures.

Sam: If node appears flappy we should failover the replica to standby and rebuild. I'll start snapshot+failover prep (taking snapshot now). Estimated time ~12m for snapshot + promote standby.

Maya (oncall): Also enabling routing fallback for regen endpoints to cached variant (10% -> 10% traffic split) to reduce write load. Note: this increases latency for some paths. Watch p99.

Nora (sre): I created the incident doc and added initial customer impact notes + timeline: https://incidents.redwood/1718880000. Tagging postmortem template.

Maya (oncall): Handoff summary for incoming shift (please keep in this thread):
- Primary at handoff: Nora (sre) will take over at 07:30 UTC.
- Secondary: Sam (on-call secondary).
- Status now: tokenstore-replica-2 unresponsive, node 10.4.2.21 cordoned and draining, consumers scaled to 6, model-router ASG +2 nodes, routing fallback 10% to cached-variant. Error rate ~18% (5m). Regen success ~88%.
- Mitigations in progress: snapshot + failover (Sam) ETA ~12m; node drain (Maya) in progress; keep routing fallback until backend error <10% for 10m straight.
- Escalation path: if error >30% or customer impact rises, contact eng-runtime pager and consider Dedicated pool warmup and permanent routing change.
- Runbook pointers: tokenstore-evictions, router-fallback-playbook, customer-regen-mitigation (links in incident doc).

Maya (oncall): Quick checklist I ran (added to doc):
- scaled consumers -> done
- triggered ASG bump -> done
- enabled 10% cached routing -> done
- cordoned node 10.4.2.21 -> in progress
- snapshot + failover -> in progress (Sam)

Nora (sre): Ack. I'll take primary at handoff and continue monitoring p50/p95/p99 and error rate. If failover fails, I'll loop in DB team and eng-runtime.

Sam: Ack. Phone on and ready to run failover steps if Nora needs me.

incident-bot: Thread appended to incident timeline. Automated alerts will continue to post here.

Maya (oncall): Final handoff note: last check error rate 18% over 5m, regen success 88%. I updated the incident doc with exact commands and logs I ran. Passing primary to @Nora at 07:30 UTC. Good handoff. :white_check_mark:

Nora (sre): Taking over. Will post status updates hourly or on major changes.
